---
title: Next.js
description: Type-safe environment variables for Next.js with zod-config/nextjs.
icon: Nextjs
---

`zod-config/nextjs` fixes the client prefix to `NEXT_PUBLIC_`.

## Define the schema

```ts twoslash title="src/env.ts"
import { loadEnvConfig } from 'zod-config/nextjs';
import { z } from 'zod';

export const env = loadEnvConfig({
  // server-only, read from process.env
  server: {
    DATABASE_URL: z.url(), // Zod 3: z.string().url()
    PORT: z.coerce.number().default(3000),
  },
  // available in the browser, keys must start with NEXT_PUBLIC_
  client: {
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL: z.url(),
  },
  // read on both sides, without the prefix
  shared: {
    NODE_ENV: z.enum(['development', 'test', 'production']),
  },
  // one entry per client and shared key, so Next.js can inline the values
  runtimeEnv: {
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL,
    NODE_ENV: process.env.NODE_ENV,
  },
});
```

`runtimeEnv` needs one entry per `client` and `shared` key, written as `process.env.NAME`: Next.js only inlines a variable into the browser bundle where the code writes it out in full. The types check that every one is listed.

## Use it

```ts
import { env } from '@/env';

env.PORT; // number
env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL; // string, on the server and in the browser
env.DATABASE_URL; // string on the server, throws in the browser
```

An invalid environment throws an `Error` that lists each invalid variable and why. See [errors and options](/docs/env#errors).

## Validate when Next.js starts

By default, `env.ts` is checked the first time it is imported, so `next dev` starts even with a missing variable and only fails when a page uses it. To check it when `next dev` or `next build` starts, choose **one** of these options.

<Tabs items={['Import the file', 'Wrap the config', 'Run it with jiti']}>
  <Tab value="Import the file">

With `next.config.ts` and no path aliases such as `@/` in `env.ts`. Nothing to install.

```ts title="next.config.ts"
import './src/env';
import type { NextConfig } from 'next';

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {};

export default nextConfig;
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Wrap the config">

With `next.config.js` / `.mjs`, or path aliases in `env.ts`. The wrapper finds `env.ts` in `src/` or the project root, runs it with [jiti](https://github.com/unjs/jiti), and returns your config unchanged. Path aliases come from the `paths` of `tsconfig.json`.

```ts twoslash title="next.config.mjs"
import { withZodConfigEnv } from 'zod-config/nextjs/config';

export default withZodConfigEnv({
  // your Next.js config
});
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Run it with jiti">

For the same cases as the wrapper, without it.

```ts title="next.config.mjs"
import { createJiti } from 'jiti';

await createJiti(import.meta.url, { tsconfigPaths: true }).import('./src/env.ts');

export default {
  // your Next.js config
};
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

- `next build` fails before compiling, with the same `Invalid environment variables` message.
- `next dev` reports the error and exits at startup.
- Values from `.env` files work: Next.js loads them before reading the config.
- It works together with [`skipValidation`](#building-without-secrets): with `SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=true`, the build still runs.

To use the wrapper or jiti by hand, install `jiti` as a regular dependency, since `next start` needs it too:

```package-install
jiti
```

### Deploying

`next start` reads `next.config` too, so with any of the three options it validates again at start, and `env.ts` (plus `jiti`, for the wrapper) must be among the deployed files. With `output: "standalone"`, the server does not read `next.config` at start: it needs neither, and the environment is validated on the first request that imports `env.ts`.

### Monorepos

The wrapper looks for `env.ts` from the working directory. When you run `next build apps/web` from the repository root, pass an absolute path:

```ts twoslash title="apps/web/next.config.mjs"
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { withZodConfigEnv } from 'zod-config/nextjs/config';

export default withZodConfigEnv(
  {},
  { file: fileURLToPath(new URL('./src/env.ts', import.meta.url)) },
);
```

jiti and `tsconfig.json` are then taken from the package that holds that file.

## Building without secrets

When secrets are not available during `next build`, skip validation for the build:

```bash
SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=true next build
```

```ts
export const env = loadEnvConfig({
  // ...
  skipValidation: process.env.SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION === 'true',
});
```

With `skipValidation`, raw values are returned without validation, coercion, transforms or defaults. The inferred types still describe the validated output, so they may not match the values.

<Callout type="warn">
  Render pages that read these secrets at request time, for example with `await connection()` from `next/server`. Next.js renders static pages once, during `next build`. With validation skipped, a static page that reads a missing secret saves `undefined` into its HTML, and no error is shown.
</Callout>
